title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning Jurisdiction and Application of Law in Trademark Cases after the Implementation of the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law

articles.content_en: Article 2: Administrative cases challenging reexamination decisions or rulings made by the National Intellectual Property Administration and cases concerning administrative acts relating to trademarks made by the National Intellectual Property Administration shall be under the jurisdiction of the relevant Intermediate People's Courts in Beijing.

Article 3: First-instance civil trademark cases shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Courts at or above the intermediate level and the Primary People's Courts designated by the Supreme People's Court.
Civil and administrative cases involving the protection of well-known trademarks shall be under the jurisdiction of the Intermediate People's Courts in the cities where the people's governments of provinces and autonomous regions are located, in the cities specifically designated in the state plan, and in the municipal districts of municipalities directly under the Central Government, and other Intermediate People's Courts designated by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 4: Where, during the process of an administrative department investigating and handling an act of infringement of trademark rights, a party brings a civil action concerning the ownership of the relevant trademark or the infringement of trademark rights, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 5: For trademark registration and renewal applications filed before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration, after the Decision comes into force, makes a decision not to accept the trademark application or not to renew it, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall apply the amended Trademark Law when reviewing the case.
For trademark opposition applications filed before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration, after the Decision comes into force, makes a decision not to accept the opposition, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall apply the pre-amendment Trademark Law when reviewing the case.

Article 6: For an application for reexamination of a trademark not yet approved for registration, filed by a party before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration makes a reexamination decision or ruling after the Decision comes into force, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall apply the amended Trademark Law when reviewing the case.
For a trademark reexamination application accepted before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration, after the Decision comes into force, makes a decision approving the registration, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall not accept the case; where the National Intellectual Property Administration, after the Decision comes into force, makes a decision not approving the registration, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall apply the pre-amendment Trademark Law when reviewing issues concerning the right of action and subject qualification.

Article 7: For trademarks that have already been approved for registration before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration accepted the application before the Decision comes into force and made a reexamination decision or ruling after the Decision comes into force, and the party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall apply the amended Trademark Law when reviewing procedural issues and the pre-amendment Trademark Law when reviewing substantive issues.

Article 8: For relevant trademark cases accepted before the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the National Intellectual Property Administration makes a decision or ruling after the Decision comes into force, and a party brings an administrative action, the People's Court shall, when determining whether the decision or ruling complies with the provisions of the Trademark Law concerning time limits for examination, calculate the examination time limit from the date on which the Decision on Amendment comes into force.

Article 9: Except as otherwise provided in this Interpretation, for civil trademark cases accepted by the People's Court after the Decision on Amending the Trademark Law comes into force, where the case involves acts that occurred before the Decision comes into force, the provisions of the pre-amendment Trademark Law shall apply; where the case involves acts that occurred before the Decision comes into force and continued after the Decision comes into force, the provisions of the amended Trademark Law shall apply.
